outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Historical Context of LSTMs
outline.description: Introduces the origins of LSTM networks, their core concepts, and why they have been pivotal in sequence modelling before the rise of Transformers.
subtopics: The vanishing gradient problem in RNNs
Constant error carousel and gating mechanisms
Original LSTM equations and intuition
Historical successes of LSTMs across domains
Limitations that led to the development of Transformers

outline.chapter_title: Fundamentals of the Standard LSTM Cell
outline.description: Provides a detailed mathematical description of the classic LSTM, establishing notation used throughout the book.
subtopics: Scalar memory cell and gate formulations
Parameterization (weights, biases, recurrent connections)
Activation functions and normalisation (tanh, sigmoid)
Multi‑cell vectorised LSTM and hidden‑hidden mixing
Ablation insights on gate importance

outline.chapter_title: Limitations of Traditional LSTMs for Large‑Scale Language Modelling
outline.description: Analyzes three key shortcomings that hinder scaling LSTMs to billions of parameters and motivates new design choices.
subtopics: Inability to revise stored information (nearest‑neighbor search example)
Restricted storage capacity – scalar vs. rich representations (rare‑token prediction)
Sequential bottleneck due to hidden‑hidden connections
Comparison with Transformer and State‑Space Model capabilities

outline.description: Introduces exponential gate activations, explains why they enable revision of memories, and details numerical stabilisation techniques.
subtopics: Exponential vs. sigmoid gate activations
Derivation of the normaliser state nₜ
Stabiliser state mₜ and log‑space formulation
'Forget' as decay and 'Input' as learning rate
Proof that stabilisation preserves forward/backward passes

outline.chapter_title: sLSTM: Scalar Memory with Mixing and Heads
outline.description: Presents the sLSTM variant, its forward equations, memory‑mixing mechanism, and multi‑head extension.
subtopics: sLSTM update equations with exponential gates
"Memory mixing" across cells via recurrent matrices
Multiple heads: independent mixing per head, shared gating
Effect of exponential gating on state tracking tasks
Implementation details (CUDA scan kernel) and computational cost

outline.chapter_title: mLSTM: Matrix Memory and Covariance Updates
outline.description: Describes the matrix‑memory design, its connection to associative memories, and how it achieves high storage capacity while remaining parallelisable.
subtopics: From scalar to d×d matrix cell Cₜ
Key‑value formulation (kₜ , vₜ) and query retrieval
Covariance (outer‑product) update rule and optimality
Normaliser vector nₜ for scaling the retrieved output
Parallel implementation and relation to Fast Weight Programmers

outline.`chapter_title`: xLSTM Blocks: Residual Architectures with Up‑Projection
outline.`description`: Shows how sLSTM or mLSTM cells are wrapped inside modern residual blocks, distinguishing post‑ and pre‑up‑projection designs.
`subtopics`: `Cover’s theorem` motivation for high‑dimensional embeddings
`Post up‑projection` block for sLSTM (non‑linear summarisation before expansion)
`Pre up‑projection` block for mLSTM (expansion before non‑linearity)
`LayerNorm` placement (pre‑LayerNorm) and residual connections
`Full xLSTM block diagram` with all sub‑components

outline.`chapter_title`: `xLSTM Architecture: Stacking Blocks into Large Models`
outline.`description`: `How multiple xLSTM blocks are stacked, how ratios of mLSTM/sLSTM blocks are chosen (xLSTM[a:b]), and overall model scaling.`
`subtopics`: `Block ratio notation xLSTM[a:b]` and design choices
`Residual stacking strategy (depth, width, embedding size)`
`Parameter budget allocation between gates, projections, and matrix memory`
`Comparison of memory & compute complexity vs. Transformers/SSMs`

outline.`description`: `Practical guidelines for training xLSTMs at scale: data preprocessing, optimisation tricks, mixed precision, and hyper‑parameter schedules.`
`subtopics`: `Dataset used (SlimPajama) and tokenisation`
`Loss function & autoregressive objective`
`Learning rate schedule, warmup, weight decay`
`Mixed precision & gradient checkpointing`
`Stabilising forget‑gate initialisation`

outline.`chapter_title`: `Synthetic Benchmarks: Verifying Exponential Gating & Memory Capacity`
outline.`description`: `Experiments that isolate the contributions of sLSTM/mLSTM on controlled tasks such as formal languages, nearest neighbor search, multi‑query associative recall, and Long Range Arena.`
`subtopics`: `State tracking tasks – parity, copy‐repeat – why Transformers fail`
`Associative recall with up to 256 key/value pairs – matrix memory advantage`
`Long Range Arena results – handling sequences up to 16k tokens`
`Analysis of accuracy vs. context length extrapolation`

outline.`chapter_title`: `Scaling Experiments on Real Language Data (15 B Tokens)`
outline.`description`: `Comprehensive comparison of xLSTM against Transformers, SSMs, and recent RNN variants when trained on a modestly sized token corpus.`
`subtopics`: `Perplexity results on validation set`
`Ablation study: adding residual backbone → up‑projection → exponential gating → matrix memory`
`Impact of different gating formulations (learnable vs. fixed)`
`Scaling curve analysis following Kaplan & Brown methodology`

outline.`chapter_title`: `Large‑Scale Language Modeling (300 B Tokens) & Downstream Evaluation`
outline.`description`: `Results when training billion‑parameter xLSTMs; includes context length extrapolation, downstream benchmark performance, PALOMA domain analysis, and scaling law extrapolation.`
`subtopics`: `Sequence length extrapolation up to 16 k tokens`
Validation perplexity across model sizes (125 M – 1.3 B)
Downstream tasks (common‑sense reasoning, ARC etc.)
PALOMA benchmark – per‑domain perplexities
Scaling law plots – offset vs. other families
Inference speed & throughput comparison with Transformer cache & Mamba

outline.`description`: Critical discussion of current bottlenecks—parallelism of sLSTM, CUDA kernel efficiency, memory growth with long contexts—and avenues for improvement.
`subtopics`: `sLSTM parallelism trade‑off
Optimising mLSTM kernels (FlashAttention style)
Reducing d×d matrix cost via low‑rank approximations
Adaptive forget‑gate initialisation strategies
Extending xLSTM to multimodal or RL settings

outline.`chapter_title`: Conclusion: Reimagining Recurrent Models for the Era of LLMs
outline.`description`: Summarises key takeaways—how exponential gating and matrix memory close the gap with Transformers—and highlights the broader impact of xLSTM.
`subtopics`: `Recap of contributions (exponential gating, sLSTM & mLSTM)
Performance relative to state-of-the-art
Implications for energy‑efficient inference
Open research questions
